description: Team Debug Dreamer's unites BCA, B.Com, BBA, and B.Tech students. We tackle the "Field Shift" challenge using NASA Earth data. Our tech unit builds an AI/ML smart irrigation prototype, while our business unit drives viability. We transform satellite data into farmer hope, aiming for the "Most Inspirational" award.
summary: AgroShift AI is a climate-aware agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers make better-informed crop planning decisions using NASA Earth observation data. It retrieves location-based historical climate information from NASA POWER, including temperature, precipitation and solar radiation. Farmers can enter their soil characteristics, current crop, irrigation conditions and farming priorities to explore alternative crop rotation strategies. A transparent multi-criteria scoring model compares four crop sequences based on water needs, soil considerations, crop diversity, climate suitability and nitrogen-related factors. The platform combines accessible climate information with farm-specific inputs to make agricultural planning easier to understand. Its goal is to encourage informed, water-conscious and climate-resilient farming decisions, particularly in agricultural regions such as Punjab, India.
details:
AgroShift AI – Project Details

1. Problem Statement

Farmers face increasing challenges from changing climate conditions, water availability and soil management. Agricultural decisions often require combining climate information with local farm conditions. AgroShift AI aims to make this information easier to explore through a simple web-based decision-support platform.

2. How the Project Works

AgroShift AI combines three main information layers:

A. NASA Earth Data
The application connects to the NASA POWER Daily API to retrieve location-specific historical temperature, precipitation and solar radiation information. Users can select a farm location using geographic coordinates and explore climate trends.

B. Farm Information
Users can enter their farm location, current crop, soil type, soil pH, organic carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, irrigation source and farming priorities.

C. Crop Rotation Decision Support
A transparent weighted multi-criteria model compares four candidate crop sequences:

  • Conventional rice–wheat baseline
  • Legume diversification
  • Water-conscious mixed rotation
  • Lower-water alternative

The model provides comparative scores and explanations based on water requirements, soil considerations, crop diversity, climate suitability and nitrogen-related factors.

3. Main Features

  • Interactive farm location map
  • NASA POWER climate data explorer
  • Temperature, rainfall and solar radiation visualizations
  • Soil and farm profile inputs
  • Crop rotation comparison and recommendations
  • Farming priority selection
  • Farm economics information

4. Technology Used

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • HTML5
  • CSS3
  • JavaScript
  • Leaflet maps
  • Chart.js visualizations
  • NASA POWER API
  • Render cloud hosting
  • GitHub version control

5. Innovation

The project connects NASA climate information with farmer-entered soil and farm details in one accessible interface. Instead of presenting climate data alone, it helps users compare alternative crop rotations using an explainable scoring approach.

6. Intended Impact

AgroShift AI aims to support more informed agricultural planning, encourage water-conscious crop choices and improve awareness of climate-related farming risks. It is designed as a decision-support prototype, not a replacement for local agricultural experts, laboratory soil testing or official agronomic recommendations.

7. Limitations

Crop rotation scores are comparative prototype indicators, not guaranteed yield forecasts, probabilities or profit predictions. NASA POWER gridded climate estimates are regional indicators rather than direct measurements from individual fields. Local validation is important before using recommendations in actual farming.
